sources.entry: vChewing 唯音 - Chinese input method supporting Pinyin and Zhuyin with purpose-built dictionaries. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/vChewing/vChewing-macOS) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: vChewing (唯音) is a native macOS input method for Traditional and Simplified Chinese supporting Zhuyin (Bopomofo) and Pinyin input, with its own dictionaries and engines.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes vChewing as a third-party native input method for macOS covering both Simplified and Traditional Chinese, with Zhuyin (Bopomofo) layouts and Pinyin input modes. It claims support for more Zhuyin layouts and input Pinyin schemes than other Zhuyin IMEs, and a Pinyin mode with a smart-Pinyin style typing experience. It uses its own Zhuyin/Pinyin engine (鐵恨注音並擊) and the Homa composition engine (formerly Megrez, moved to LibVanguard in 2026). Optional features named include an on-screen keyboard for certain layouts, output conversion to Japanese JIS shinjitai or Kangxi forms, separate Simplified and Traditional corpora, and Shift-key language toggling. The README also describes a sandboxed build and a web-based configuration assistant (TypeScript compiled to a single HTML file) that is optional to build. Build instructions use make targets (update, release, archive, debug) and require Swift 6.4+ toolchain and Xcode.
use_cases: type Chinese on a Mac with Zhuyin/Bopomofo
type Chinese on a Mac with Pinyin
use a Traditional Chinese input method on macOS
build a custom macOS Chinese input method from source
customize phrase dictionaries for Chinese input
use a sandboxed third-party Chinese IME
how_to_run: Clone the repository and cd into the local project directory
make update  (fetch latest dictionary resources via remote Swift Package plugin)
make release  (build universal arm64 + x86_64 binary into Build/Products/Release/)
Alternatively open the Xcode project, select the vChewingInstaller scheme, and build
notable: Own Zhuyin engine (鐵恨注音並擊) and Homa composition engine (LGPL v3.0 or later)
Sandboxed app that the README says cannot obtain system-wide keyboard permission
Separate Simplified and Traditional Chinese corpora
Optional web-based configuration assistant that produces importable config packs
Claims support for a large number of Zhuyin layouts and Pinyin schemes
caveats: Building requires Swift 6.4+; on Intel Macs this needs Xcode 26.x plus a separate open-source Swift toolchain, and Xcode cannot use that toolchain to resolve packages
Shift-key Chinese/English switching requires macOS 10.15 Catalina or later
Some README content is in Traditional Chinese and the Gitee mirror is named as the place with up-to-date content
